title: Velocity-based pricing and soft overdraft acceptance criteria
creator: Ava Chen
description: Introduce a velocity-based pricing layer and a soft overdraft (grace) mechanism to reduce customer friction during short bursts and enable predictable cost controls. The feature should allow customers to consume beyond their plan quota for a limited time window (soft overdraft), be billed transparently, and optionally fall back to lower-cost model variants when budget thresholds are reached.
background: We receive frequent support tickets from customers whose production traffic spikes cause sudden throttles or unexpected overage invoices. Current per-window quotas and hard rate-limits are simple but inflexible. Velocity-based pricing (charging partially by short-term usage velocity) combined with a soft overdraft will allow short bursts without immediate hard failures, while preserving safety controls to prevent runaway spend. This ties to ongoing work on per-route entitlements and per-caller concurrency pools.
goals: Reduce customer-visible 429s for short burst traffic by at least 60% for customers on paid tiers
Provide transparent billing and invoice line items for soft overdraft usage
Enable automatic model fallback to lower-cost variants when sustained overdraft is detected
Ensure billing accuracy to within 0.5% for velocity-charged tokens over a billing cycle
Ship operator and product dashboards for diagnosing overdraft events and velocity trends
in_scope: Define velocity metric (tokens/minute and tokens/second buckets) and pricing tiers
Implement soft overdraft policy engine with configurable grace window and soft-cap limit per tenant
Billing pipeline changes to produce per-tenant overdraft line items and reconciliation hooks
API and SDK surface: new headers and response codes indicating overdraft state and fallback triggers
Console UX: an overdraft dashboard, alerting rule templates, and per-route velocity visualization
Acceptance criteria and automated test harness for metering and charge calculation
out_of_scope: Major billing system rearchitect (only extend current pipeline with adapters)
Free-tier unlimited bursts (soft overdraft available only to paid plans)
Per-user seat billing changes unrelated to token/velocity metering
Enterprise contractual crediting policies (handled via legal/finance exceptions)
Backend model-level optimization (quantization/recompilation) as part of this ticket
requirements: R1: Velocity metric: system must compute rolling 1s, 30s, 5m, and 1h token velocity per tenant with <200ms tail latency for read operations
R2: Soft overdraft policy: configurable parameters: grace_window_seconds, soft_cap_tokens, overdraft_rate_multiplier, max_overdraft_duration_seconds
R3: Billing: produce line items for overdraft with fields: start_ts, end_ts, tokens_charged, velocity_tier, price_per_token
R4: Fallback: support deterministic fallback policy that switches to a lower-cost model variant after sustained overdraft (configurable threshold in minutes)
R5: API behavior: when in soft overdraft state, responses include header 'X-Overdraft-State' with values 'ok'|'soft'|'sustained', and 'X-Overdraft-Reason' for human-readable reason codes
R6: Rate-limit semantics: hard rate-limits still enforce absolute max tokens/sec for safety; soft overdraft allows temporary exceed of plan quotas within configured bounds
R7: Telemetry: emit events for overdraft_start, overdraft_end, overdraft_escalation, fallback_initiated with tenant id and rolling velocity metrics
R8: Migration: tiered rollout with opt-in flag for accounts; default to opt-out to avoid surprising charges for legacy plans
acceptance_criteria: AC1: For a test tenant with plan quota Q and soft_cap_tokens S, simulate a 10x short burst for 90s. System should allow requests until S is consumed and then return 429 if hard safety limit reached
AC2: Billing pipeline emits correct overdraft line items for simulated bursts: total tokens equals measured usage within 0.5% and price_per_token applied according to velocity tier mapping
AC3: Console shows overdraft events on tenant timeline with links to raw metering and per-route breakdown within 60s of event detection
AC4: API responses during soft overdraft include correct headers and documentation; SDK sample updated and validated via integration test

AC5: Fallback to lower-cost model triggers after configured sustained_overdraft_minutes and traffic is routed to fallback variant with no data loss; fallback and return-to-primary are observable in logs and dashboard

AC6: Billing reconciliation e2e: run a 48h synthetic workload that includes multiple bursts; finance-runner script reconciles generated line items against ingestion store with zero mismatches in token totals
AC7: Alerting: on-call receives alert if a tenant consumes >3x soft_cap_tokens within 1h and projected monthly spend delta > $5000
AC8: Backwards compatibility: enabling overdraft for an account does not change billing for accounts without the feature flag enabled
monitoring_and_metrics: Metric: overdraft_active_count (number of tenants currently in soft overdraft)
Metric: overdraft_tokens_total (tokens charged via overdraft) by tenant and by plan
Dashboard: per-tenant overdraft timeline with model variant toggles
Logs: structured events with reason codes for automated audits
SLOs: billing accuracy pipeline success rate >= 99.9% per billing run
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design review and security/finance signoff; create feature flag and test harness
Phase 1: Internal dogfood rollout (10 internal tenants) for 2 weeks with active monitoring
Phase 2: Opt-in beta for selected customers (sales-marketing curated list) for 6 weeks
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to all paid customers with communication plan and billing preview emails 7 days before enabling
Phase 4: Full GA with SDK docs, example clients, and updated pricing FAQ
risks: Unexpected invoice shocks for customers if opt-in semantics are miscommunicated
Metering divergence between real-time counters and billing batch may cause temporary discrepancies
Performance impact: computing multiple rolling velocity windows could add CPU/DB load if not optimized
Complexity in fallback routing might increase tail latency for some requests
Legal/compliance concerns if overdraft is enabled for regulated customers without explicit consent
dependencies: ENG-42011 (metering infra: high-cardinality time-series store for tokens)
ENG-44120 (billing pipeline: line-item adapter for overdraft events)
